query: This is our nightly transcode job. Quality complaints keep coming in and it falls over on some clips with an encoder error. Review it and fix whatever is actually wrong.
expected_behavior: Says the VP9 command needs `-b:v 0` alongside `-crf`, and explains that without it the encoder can silently run Constrained Quality instead of constant quality rather than merely 'it is recommended'

Identifies `scale=1280:-1` as the cause of the encoder failure — it can compute an odd height, which libx264 with yuv420p rejects — and changes it to `scale=1280:-2` rather than hardcoding a height or switching to `-s`
Removes the `setsar=1` after `scale`, stating that `scale` preserves the source SAR and that forcing SAR 1:1 corrupts the display aspect ratio of the anamorphic 640x480 source
Moves `-ss 00:01:30` before `-i` for the preview, and does not claim output-side seeking is required for frame accuracy when re-encoding
Surfaces `-preset veryslow` as a deliberate cost decision with its rough encode-time multiple against `medium`, instead of silently keeping it or silently changing it
Adds `-movflags +faststart` to the MP4 deliverables intended for web playback
Runs or prescribes `ffprobe` on a source to establish resolution, SAR/DAR, frame rate and codecs before changing the commands, instead of rewriting the script from the source text alone

query: Players stutter and sometimes go black for a second when the network makes them switch quality on our lecture videos. Segment lengths in the playlists are also all over the place — some are 6 seconds, some are 11. This is the packaging script.
expected_behavior: Names unaligned keyframes across the three renditions as the cause of the switching artefacts: each encode picks its own scene-change keyframes, so the player has no common splice point

Fixes it by forcing a fixed GOP across all renditions — `-g` and `-keyint_min` set to framerate times segment duration with `-sc_threshold 0`, or `-force_key_frames` on a time expression — and uses identical settings for every rendition
Explains the varying segment lengths as `hls_time` being a lower bound that the muxer can only cut on a keyframe, not an exact duration

Addresses variable frame rate in the phone-shot sources: a VFR input makes 'framerate times segment duration' meaningless, so the frame rate is pinned (`-r`/`fps` filter) or the keyframe expression is driven by timestamps rather than frame counts
Points out that `-b:v` together with `-crf` on libx264 is not the rate control an ABR ladder needs, and picks one — capped CRF with `-maxrate`/`-bufsize`, or two-pass ABR — per rendition

Says the master playlist BANDWIDTH values must reflect the measured peak bitrate of each rendition rather than being copied from the requested `-b:v`, and that RESOLUTION must match what was actually produced
Verifies by probing the produced segments — reporting actual segment durations and keyframe positions across renditions — instead of trusting `-hls_time`

query: Thumbnails from this script come out sideways for a lot of the photos, and the studio shots look washed out on the product pages. Sort it out.
expected_behavior: Names the root cause as ffmpeg not carrying EXIF through to the output — the Orientation tag is gone from the thumbnail, so nothing downstream can rotate it
Moves still-image work off ffmpeg onto an image tool (vips, sharp, ImageMagick or Pillow) instead of keeping ffmpeg and compensating inside it with hand-built rotation and colour-conversion machinery
Justifies the tool switch on cost: the image tools apply orientation and ICC conversion as one documented call, and the alternative is reimplementing colour management by hand
Applies orientation explicitly (`vips` autorotate, `sharp.autoOrient()`, `magick -auto-orient` or `ImageOps.exif_transpose`) rather than assuming the new tool does it silently

Explains the washed-out studio shots as a colour-management problem: the Display-P3 ICC profile is discarded or ignored, so wide-gamut pixels are interpreted as sRGB, and converts to sRGB deliberately
Does not carry `-q:v 2` across as if it were the same scale as `-quality`/`quality:` in the image tool
Re-reads a converted output file and reports its dimensions, orientation and colour profile as the check, rather than asserting the fix works

query: Our product images load slowly on mobile. We serve them from cdn.example.com through next/image. Tune the Next.js image config so mobile gets smaller files.
expected_behavior: Does not read skills/media-processing/SKILL.md
Answers with Next.js image configuration (deviceSizes/imageSizes, formats, sizes prop on the component) rather than opening an ffmpeg or ImageMagick workflow
Treats this as framework-owned image pipeline work instead of a local media processing job
